dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (CIDP) with cranial nerve involvement

The constellation of findings — chronic progressive course, demyelinating sensorimotor neuropathy on nerve conduction studies, elevated CSF protein with normal cell count (albuminocytologic dissociation), multiple cranial nerve enhancement and thickening on MRI, and absent reflexes — fits the diagnostic criteria for CIDP. The cranial nerve involvement (III–XII thickening) represents the cranial variant or cranial predilection that can occur in this condition, explaining the ocular motility deficits, ptosis, and heel-walking difficulty.
